overall_reason: An untinted grey scale carries the task card (#222222 title, #444444 names, #999999 on 10 elements for metadata, the count and the status), with a hairline under the header and between each row.

score.reason: T-NEUTRALS passes with one temperature; T-LINE-DELETION finds rules that spacing already does, and T-PALETTE-ROLES finds status in the same grey as metadata.

findings.title: Draw lines only to separate regions, encode state, or carry data
findings.evidence: The card draws a hairline under 'Project tasks' and between each of the 3 rows inside a bordered card. Hiding the row rules leaves the rows grouped by their spacing.
findings.before: A rule on every row inside a bordered card.
findings.after: Rows separated by space, with one rule under the header at most.
findings.why: Lines that carry no structure add noise to a short list.

findings.title: State colours keep their meaning
findings.evidence: The text roles list #999999 on 10 small elements: the count '3 open', names with dates, and both status labels.
findings.before: Status values share the metadata grey.
findings.after: Status in ink or a state colour with its word, distinct from metadata.
findings.why: The status, the thing a reader scans for, has no colour role of its own.

strengths: One untinted grey family with no shadows.
not_investigated: T-DARK-MODE: the page renders light; the stylesheet has a dark class theme that the capture did not render, so dark mode is not verified
brand authority: the run has no 00-contract.md, so no brand colours were available for T-COLOUR-SOURCE; sources were traced from the composition itself
contrast and focus: owned by the sweep (A11-001, A11-003) and not restated here
